hook_text: A pot of relish is a factory line: things in, steps, food out. Draw the line before you light the gas.
clip_script: Kitchen as factory. Inputs: tins, onions, oil. Processes: wash, chop, fry, open, add, simmer, season. Output: ten plates, steaming hot. Now the steps, each with a verb, a time and a name. Wash hands. Wipe the surface. Chop the onions before the oil is hot. Fry five minutes. Diamond: soft? No, two more minutes. Open the tomato, add. Open the pilchards, add gently. Salt, spice. Simmer ten. Diamond: seasoned? No, a pinch more. Diamond: steaming hot? Serve. Hygiene gets boxes: soap, separate boards, cover the food. Safety gets boxes: blade away, lid by the edge, dry cloth, handle turned in. Add up the minutes. Fit the period. Four roles. Walk it through once. Then cook it with nobody asking what comes next.
visual_style: Whiteboard column of boxes filling with verbs and minutes; three diamonds branching and looping; hygiene and safety boxes highlighted; times summing at the bottom.
mood: Brisk and careful, a kitchen running like clockwork.
pacing: Inputs, steps, diamonds, hygiene, safety, sum, roles, each a beat.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and draw the sequence for one dish you cook at home.
